features.behavior: From font-family, lang and loaded web fonts, predict per platform (mac, windows, ios, android) which region's font draws Han text.
Tell Japanese, Chinese and Korean text apart by script counts, and other languages down to their script.
Turn an analysed page into han-font, lang-mismatch, lang-missing, wrong-language and page-error findings, a verdict, report version 1 and an exit code.
cjk-sense check accepts URLs, --urls-file, --expect, --platforms, --fail-on, --format and --out, and exits 0, 1 or 2; cjk-sense --version prints the package version.
features.verify: uv run --quiet --no-project --with-requirements requirements-gate.txt pytest -q tests services/snapshot/tests

features.behavior: In Chromium on macOS the 22 known-answer pages give exactly the expected rules, and every font prediction that names a region matches the font the browser used (predictions of 'system' are counted but accept any font).

In Edge on Windows 11 the 22 known-answer pages give exactly the expected rules, and every font prediction that names a region matches the font the browser used (predictions of 'system' are counted but accept any font).
features.note: Must run on Windows; it cannot be verified from macOS or Linux, so the state stays blocked here. Last run: 22/22 on 2026-11-20 on Windows 11 with Edge, on the code of that day, output kept in docs/records/windows-eval-2026-11-20.txt. Rerun on Windows after any change to the behaviour of fonts_lib.py, snapshot_lib.py, detect_lib.py, check_lib.py or cjk_sense/cli.py.

features.behavior: The sdist and the wheel hold exactly the expected files and metadata and pass twine check; each, installed into a clean environment, prints its version and usage, checks pages served over HTTP in a real browser and returns the right verdicts and exit codes.

The rules for what may be published are pinned: exact file lists and metadata of wheel and sdist (no email address, no README link PyPI cannot follow), one version in pyproject.toml, the package and the changelog, workflow actions pinned to commits, and a release workflow that publishes only on a GitHub release or by hand, without a token.
